prs.author: Epochex

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder.cancel() in shared/session.py sends an inappropriate error response when a request is cancelled, violating the JSON-RPC/MCP spec rule that receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request. Both PRs edit the exact same cancel() method (adjacent hunks, lines ~141-159) to fix this. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: #2514 is the more complete fix: it removes the same incorrect error-response code but replaces it with a spec-compliant `notifications/cancelled` notification (adds CancelledNotificationParams import) and covers both the request-timeout and caller-initiated cancellation paths, not just the client-CancelledNotification case. #2493's server.py hunk is a comment/log-message-only change with no behavioral difference from existing code, and its session.py hunk is purely subtractive (removes the bad send with no replacement), leaving the timeout/caller-cancellation scenarios unaddressed. #2514 also drops a `# pragma: no cover` marker on the entered-check, indicating it adds test coverage for a path #2493 leaves untested.

clusters.pick_reason: Both patch the identical raise sites in auth/utils.py and session.py, so they will conflict on merge. #2777 goes further by also dropping the redundant f"{e}" interpolation from the message text (since `from e` already preserves the original exception in the traceback), yielding a tighter net diff (+11/-11) versus #2565's tack-on-only fix (+15/-15) that leaves the exception text duplicated in the message. #2777 also already has 1 review recorded versus 0 for #2565.

members.title: fix: chain exceptions with `from` in 12 remaining raise sites
members.author: blackwell-systems
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2777: Both PRs fix the same underlying issue: `raise` statements inside `except` blocks that don't chain the original exception via `from e`, losing traceback context (ruff B904 / PEP 3134). Both touch the exact same lines in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py (OAuthRegistrationError and OAuthTokenError raises) and both also modify src/mcp/client/session.py.
